📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A close ally of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, President Donald Trump reportedly dialed into an Nvidia board meeting to push for the ousted CEO’s return, Semafor reported on Monday. Trump got his way, as Nvidia announced Huang’s reinstatement shortly afterward.

“I spoke to them, let me put it that way … And I convinced them,” the president told CNBC.

Huang was forced to step down from his role as CEO, which he held for 33 years, after news broke that he had affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees, including a direct report.

“President Trump was totally involved and this is a great decision by the NVIDIA board. We have to protect our geniuses,” White House communications director Steven Cheung told Semafor.

The president took to his social media app, Truth Social, to remark that “the United States government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to Nvidia poses any risk to national security.”.

According to Nvidia’s press release about Huang’s reinstatement as CEO and president, the company claimed that “the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.”.

While Trump has declared that Huang “did absolutely nothing wrong,” many government officials aren’t buying the president’s point of view. Huang is still expected to testify in closed-door conversations with three committees of the House of Representatives on December 1. He is also slated to appear before the Senate Banking Committee to testify publicly, though that hearing has not been scheduled yet.

“People say, is it a threat to have him? No, it’s a threat to lose him,” Trump said to CNBC.

Trump has maintained this position through the scandal, even denying that he was ever told about Huang’s relationship with an alleged Chinese spy named Alice Huang (no relation). The New York Times reported, on the contrary, that Trump’s secretary of state and national security adviser Marco Rubio briefed him aboard Air Force One in May.

Earlier this spring, Rubio also supervised the drafting of a memo that circulated among top policymakers, warning that Alice Huang was spying for China’s Ministry of State Security.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, controlling what AI agents can reach is one of the biggest constraints on enterprise AI adoption. Cymphony is building the governance and security layer that removes it.

It has been revealed that controlling what AI agents can reach is one of the biggest constraints on enterprise AI adoption. Cymphony is building the governance and security layer that removes it.

Every large enterprise now has an AI mandate. Very few know exactly what happens when an agent is granted access to enterprise systems and data. What exactly will it be able to reach? How will we know what it did with it? These questions â not model quality, not cost, not talent â are the reason so many enterprise AI programs stay stuck in pilots. Cymphony was built to answer them.

Recent findings suggest that employees increasingly work together with AI agents to execute day-to-day work. But the typical agent is nothing like an employee. It can be provisioned in minutes rather than hired over weeks. It works continuously. And it can reach across far more systems, data, and capability than an individual person. Every one of those properties is what makes an AI agent worth deploying â and every one of them is what makes a security team say no.

Governance and security are already major barriers to AI adoption, with 40% of enterprises expected to demote or decommission autonomous AI agents over governance concerns by next year. That is not a prediction about AI failing to work. Itâs about enterprises pulling back working agents because they cannot see or control what those agents reaching. The fundamental challenge is not utility, but accountability.

For decades, security teams have built tools around two separate concerns: where sensitive data lives, and who has access. The first produced the tools that watch files, inboxes, and databases for leaks. The second produced the identity industry. But both assume the "who"s are human employees.

Recent findings suggest that AI broke that assumption. An identity tool can tell you an agent exists. A data tool can tell you a file is sensitive. Neither can tell you that a given agent, acting on behalf of a given employee, can reach that file right now. Identity security and data security are no longer separable.

Sources indicate that cymphony continuously maps both employees and agents across an enterprise, graphing who and what can reach which systems and information. It is a difficult engineering problem: the same person routinely holds a dozen different accounts scattered across systems that were never designed to talk to each other, and agents inherit access from the humans and applications that spawned them. Stitching all of that back into one accurate picture requires more than a dashboard that aggregates alerts.

What we love about working with co-founders Shy Dekel, Idan Berkovits, and Edi Gotlieb is their instinct to build not for the alert but for the workflow. Instead of stopping at detection and leaving a security analyst to figure out what to do next, Cymphony pushes further â recommending and even automating remediation, and coordinating with the people who need to take action.

Enterprise customers including Syngenta, KKR, Cass Information Systems, and Athennian are already seeing results. Sequoia is also a happy customer. We are proud to have led Cymphonyâs seed round, and to now co-lead their Series A.

We met Shy, Idan, and Edi through Sequoia's Israel network, introduced separately by two people in our orbit who each stated some version of the same thing: these three had spent their careers on hard, unglamorous security problem many founders avoid, and they were building something different around it. All three came out of Israel's elite Talpiot program. All three have deep experience in this space: Shy led the cyber department for Unit 8200, Idan ran a research group in the Office of the Prime Minister and won an Israel Defense Prize, and Edi built hardware at Apple and at the Israeli Ministry of Defense. Every large enterprise software manufacturer has been built on a transition: the underlying unit of work changes, and the old categories are no longer the right shape. Cloud changed where software ran, and security rebuilt itself around it. Mobile changed what an endpoint was, and it rebuilt itself again. Each time, the companies that offered visibility and control over what came next eventually became infrastructure everyone else took for granted.

AI is no exception, albeit the first shift where the new unit of work can act on its own. The organization that lets an enterprise say yes to agents â confidently, at scale, with a record of what they did â will be not just a feature inside the AI stack, but a precondition for it. We think Cymphony is building that layer, and we are glad to be part of it.

By Bogomil Balkansky, Dean Meyer and David Cahn.

#26023. Jensen Huang isn’t out of the woods yet

Jensen Huang isn’t out of the woods yet

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (854 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, monday morning, Jensen Huang returned as CEO of Nvidia, after resigning the position following news of multiple affairs, including one with a subordinate and one with a woman tied to Chinese intelligence services.
  • According to recent reports, still, tech leaders should be clear-eyed about all the problems likely to come with Huang’s reinstatement.
  • Most importantly, serious questions remain about how Nvidia chips were smuggled into China, and how much Nvidia knew about it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s safe to say no one expected this.

In a recent development, monday morning, Jensen Huang returned as CEO of Nvidia, after resigning the position following news of multiple affairs, including one with a subordinate and one with a woman tied to Chinese intelligence services. With so much of the AI industry built on top of Nvidia’s AI infrastructure, Huang’s departure looked like an imminent threat to the business — and the mood on his return has been ecstatic. Share prices are rocketing back up, particularly for neoclouds like CoreWeave and Nebius, and the Nasdaq rose 7% on the news.

According to recent reports, still, tech leaders should be clear-eyed about all the problems likely to come with Huang’s reinstatement. President Trump is already telling reporters that the U.S. government found no national security concerns resulting from the affair, but the broader national security concerns aren’t so easy to dismiss, and Trump’s involvement may do more harm than good for Nvidia and its partners. This isn’t the end of the problems caused by Huang’s affairs; it’s likely just the beginning.

Most importantly, serious questions remain about how Nvidia chips were smuggled into China, and how much Nvidia knew about it. Among Jensen Huang’s defenders, it’s become common to question whether Alice Huang was really a spy, but it’s clear that a lot of restricted chips were flowing into China through her company. Just this weekend, The Upcoming York Times reported sustained contact between Alice Huang and a member of China’s Ministry of State Security during the same period she was having an affair with Jensen Huang.

With Democrats in control of Congress, including investigative bodies like the House Oversight Committee, there are plenty of ways to force the issue. Nvidia’s role in violating U.S. export controls would likely have been the subject of prolonged uncomfortable investigation, whether Huang returned or not. But with him back in the CEO’s seat, there will be a lot more riding on any revelations that come up — and any upcoming revelations will damage Nvidia as a company alongside Huang himself.

Then there are the questions raised by Trump’s intervention. It’s unprecedented in American history for a sitting president to intervene to clear a CEO accused of being a national security risk. Simply pressing the Department of Justice to exonerate Huang would have been a scandal, but calling the Nvidia board goes significantly further. Huang has already donated $25 million to Trump’s ballroom project, so it’s easy to make the case that Trump was intervening on behalf of a donor, setting national security risks aside for his personal benefit.

All of this is happening just as Democrats retake Congress, with all of its associated investigative powers. Even if they can’t fire Huang or remove Trump, there are lots of uncomfortable questions that are still unanswered. Was there any Department of Justice inquiry into whether Huang had committed a crime, or did Trump make the call on his own? Did the intelligence services make any official assessment that could be subpoenaed into the congressional record? Investigating Democrats will be particularly interested in Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who oversees export controls and retains significant financial ties to the industry through his firm, Cantor Fitzgerald.

If all of this sounds exhausting, you’re getting a sense of what the next year will be like for anyone following national news. Congress will keep a steady drip of embarrassing revelations, milking as much political juice as possible out of Huang and everyone associated with him. Trump will keep lashing out, often making things worse for everyone involved. (Trump’s statement to CBS, which defends Huang in racist terms while also accusing him of treason, is an early taste.) It’s going to be ugly and sad, and the most successful tech firm of the last decade will be right at the center of it.

Recent findings suggest that I have to assume that this was the scenario the board was concerned about when it decided to remove Huang two weeks ago. Since then, the cost of removing him has gone up: an open letter from Nvidia’s employees and partners, a tanking stock market, and, ultimately, direct intervention from the president of the United States.

Industry observers note that but nothing has lowered the cost of keeping Huang, and the ugly scenario the board foresaw earlier this month is still very much in place. We’re about to see it come to life.

Meta throws out its net-zero goal — its competitors should be furious

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1209 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Meta’s new sustainability report buries the lead: The organization is almost certain to miss its own goal to reach net zero by 2030, and it’s refusing to commit to a new timeline.
  • “We are re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets — so our approach reflects current operating realities while keeping progress transparent year over year,” wrote Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers at Meta, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net-zero and sustainability at Meta, in the introduction to the manufacturer’s 2026 sustainability report.
  • That’s a lot of words to say that Meta will continue to pollute if that means it can continue its AI rollout.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Meta’s new sustainability report buries the lead: The organization is almost certain to miss its own goal to reach net zero by 2030, and it’s refusing to commit to a new timeline.

“We are re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets — so our approach reflects current operating realities while keeping progress transparent year over year,” wrote Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers at Meta, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net-zero and sustainability at Meta, in the introduction to the manufacturer’s 2026 sustainability report.

That’s a lot of words to say that Meta will continue to pollute if that means it can continue its AI rollout.

It has been revealed that such is the risk of voluntary targets. Companies can make and break them with little to lose, betting — often rightly — that they can ignore them with just a small hit to public opinion, which is fickle anyway. (Remember the Cambridge Analytica scandal? Most people don’t.) There’s almost no risk to the bottom line.

In a recent development, “We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline and interim milestone. We’ll continue investing in emissions reductions and reporting our progress annually,” a Meta spokesperson told TechCrunch.

According to recent reports, A few years ago, Meta was arguably one of the better corporate stewards of the climate. The company has been one of the largest purchasers of clean power, and it set ambitious goals for water conservation.

It has been revealed that more recently, though, its multibillion-dollar bet on natural gas at its Hyperion data center in Louisiana has undone much of that progress. Natural gas may burn cleaner and more efficiently than coal, but its impact on global warming can be just as bad when the leaky infrastructure needed to burn it is factored in.

Despite years of clean power procurement, Meta’s greenhouse gas emissions have more than doubled in the last four years. Between 2024 and 2025, its data center emissions increased more than 12 times, and Hyperion isn’t online yet.

Sources indicate that that commitment to natural gas led to the manufacturer’s departure from RE100, a corporate renewable energy initiative, in July. The company had been part of the group for a decade, though the two split after RE100 started requiring more rigorous reporting toward renewable energy targets.

It has been revealed that “When we set our net zero emissions goal, we anticipated steady growth, falling clean energy costs, and changes in the broader system that would enable progress at the pace we envisioned,” they added. “The reality has been far more complex. Demand for AI infrastructure has grown faster than almost anyone projected, arriving on a timeline measured in quarters rather than decades, and meeting it has meant building at a pace and scale the industry has never attempted.”.

That’s all true, but when put that way, it sounds like Meta has little agency in the matter. But the tech giant’s decision to chase AI was a conscious one.

It has been revealed that you could argue that Meta has a fiduciary duty to chase after its peers, which have also dived headfirst into AI. But there’s precious little data to support the idea that AI will be a profit driver for a firm like Meta, which is almost entirely consumer-focused.

In a recent development, CEO Mark Zuckerberg is optimistic that improving Muse’s energy efficiency will turn that around, but how much will everyday people be willing to pay for software that translates your offhand thoughts into surreal memes? Or monitors your emails so you won’t forget to reply to your mom? Meta is betting that it’ll be enough to support a $200 billion-plus data center, and probably more.

The choice of the fuel to power those AI ambitions was also a conscious one. Natural gas power plants, besides being able to run 24/7, are actually not a great fit for AI data centers. Turbines like to run at constant speeds, while AI data centers’ energy requirements surge and sag depending on the load. They need batteries as a buffer, which begs the question: Why not just connect to the grid and use batteries to bridge any gaps during times of peak demand? That’s what one expert recommends.

According to recent reports, meta’s bet on natural gas appears mistimed. Long-duration energy storage is coming into its own — and geothermal energy appears poised to become the next major power source on the grid in the U.S. Companies like Fervo, Mazama, and Quaise have been logging milestones at a rapid clip, potentially unlocking tens of gigawatts of capacity. The technology isn’t competitive with natural gas today, but it very well could be in the mid-2030s, just a few years after Meta completes Hyperion. Geothermal is also not vulnerable to supply chain shocks, like what happened with natural gas and the Iran War.

Beyond that, the company’s decision to abandon its 2030 net-zero goal risks fomenting the sort of backlash that leads to regulations with real teeth. Such regulations won’t just apply to Meta, and the broader industry would be justified in their frustration.

It has been revealed that in that light, Meta’s timing couldn’t be worse. Surveys show the general public doesn’t hold AI or data centers in high esteem, rightly sensing that the infrastructure development is driving a rapid and often-unchecked expansion of polluting infrastructure.

Industry observers note that the tech industry has spent over a decade trying to prove that it would be different from previous industrial juggernauts like oil and gas or automobile manufacturing. In a single PDF, Meta might have undone much of that goodwill. After this, who will trust another tech company’s voluntary net-zero goals?

Amazon has agreed to acquire a good chunk of Israeli startup Decart.

The e-commerce and cloud giant is paying $7.5 billion for the startup, according to Bloomberg.

It has been revealed that decart has made a name for itself building interactive real-time world models — most recently Oasis 3 — and AI video-generation tools. But under the hood, the manufacturer stands out for its Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), software that helps AI models run efficiently on Nvidia, Amazon, and Google’s hardware.

As part of the deal, Amazon will acquire the technology behind DOS, as well as Decart’s founding team and team of AI researchers and engineers, Amazon said in a blog post.

In a recent development, “Every leap forward in AI starts with getting more out of every chip,” noted Peter DeSantis, SVP of foundational AI models, custom silicon, quantum computing, at Amazon. “More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost.”.

In a recent development, amazon, which has so far been using its Trainium chips at its own data centers, is preparing to start selling them to customers as a competitor to Nvidia. Decart’s technology could make it easier for customers to run their workloads on Amazon chips, rather than Nvidia’s, which has been the gold standard so far.

Decart and Amazon did not immediately return requests for comment.

Recent findings suggest that for years, "using AI" has mostly meant humans typing into a box and waiting for an answer. The next chapter belongs to agents. Machines chase solutions to any problem with patience and tenacity, bound only by the compute and context they are given.

In a recent development, the demand for agents is here. The infrastructure to run them ambitiously is not. Sail is the platform to run agents ambitiously.

In a recent development, sail is building for a world in which agents run for hours or days to solve our most complex problems. Sail purpose-built their inference platform to operate across a wide range of compute and flex to handle long running, agent tasks. Google Search’s AI Mode can now tap into Drive and Wallet for more personalized responses

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (545 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that google unveiled on Monday that it’s expanding Personal Intelligence in Search’s AI Mode with integrations for Google Drive, Google Wallet, and the Gemini app.
  • By bringing Personal Intelligence in AI Mode to Drive, Wallet, and the Gemini app, Google is leveraging the wealth of user data that’s already within its ecosystem.
  • According to recent reports, google says that connecting Google Wallet to Personal Intelligence lets owners track their financial goals, cut everyday spending, and make better use of credit card rewards.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that google unveiled on Monday that it’s expanding Personal Intelligence in Search’s AI Mode with integrations for Google Drive, Google Wallet, and the Gemini app. Personal Intelligence is designed to offer customers more personalized, context-aware answers by connecting to their Google apps and drawing on information from their digital lives. The feature can already connect to apps like Gmail, Google Calendar, and Google Photos.

By bringing Personal Intelligence in AI Mode to Drive, Wallet, and the Gemini app, Google is leveraging the wealth of user data that’s already within its ecosystem. Since customers rely on these services, the tech giant can deliver more personalized experiences that rivals aren’t able to match. Of course, not everyone wants AI looking at their Wallet and Drive, so connecting the apps is optional, and you can turn Personal Intelligence on or off at any time.

According to recent reports, google says that connecting Google Wallet to Personal Intelligence lets owners track their financial goals, cut everyday spending, and make better use of credit card rewards. The tech giant notes that if users choose to connect their Wallet, AI Mode can only read information from accounts and isn’t able to move or manage their money.

As for Drive, the organization indicates vital information related to a project or major decision is often scattered across documents and spreadsheets. By connecting Google Drive to Personal Intelligence, AI can draw on those files to provide more relevant, personalized answers, such as creating a tailored plan for tax season.

Customers will also be able to share context between their Gemini app and AI Mode in Search, which means that if they explore an idea in the Gemini app, they won’t have to start over with AI Mode because it will already have the information, and vice versa.

Additionally, Google says consumers will soon be able to view the context that AI Mode uses via a newly introduced “Personalization” icon that will appear below responses.

The company also declared on Monday that customers will start to see more personally relevant responses in AI Overviews and AI Mode that will be tailored to users’ recent search context.

Partnering with Mecka: Bringing AI to the Physical World

📅 07 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (921 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sequoiacap

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Josh and Jason are building the data and deployment layer for physical AI.
  • Josh and Jason are building the data and deployment layer for physical AI.
  • It has been revealed that AI took the digital world by storm in a few short years, and we are still only scratching the surface.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Josh and Jason are building the data and deployment layer for physical AI.

Josh and Jason are building the data and deployment layer for physical AI.

It has been revealed that AI took the digital world by storm in a few short years, and we are still only scratching the surface. Each time digital AI has moved to a upcoming phase, from pretraining to reinforcement learning to deployment, spend on compute and data has not plateaued. It has accelerated.

Bringing AI into the physical world will be a wave of comparable importance to digital AI, if not larger, but the infrastructure required to get there will be harder to build and scale, and that already highlights at every stage. In pretraining, language models benefited from decades of text accumulated on the internet. Robotics has no comparable, ready-made collection of the movements, interactions and sensory information needed to understand the physical world. That experience has to be captured before it can be learned from. In reinforcement learning and deployment, digital AI operates in clean, structured environments that are easy to scale. Physical AI lives in the noisy, unpredictable, operationally complex reality of the real world. It operates in the field, not in the cloud.

To reach physical AGI, the industry has to build both the brain and the body. The brain needs data that wasnât collected. The body needs someone doing the work on the ground.

That is the mission Josh, Jason and the Mecka AI team have taken on: helping physical AI labs, robotics companies and end enterprises reach physical AGI and put it to use, by being their partner for training data, reinforcement learning, and deployment.

Delivering on this mission requires developing several muscles across disciplines, all at once and all at scale:.

Research: Identify the next wave in robotics, and what it will require, before it arrives.

Hardware: Once you see the wave, design the bespoke hardware and wearables to capture the data, then manufacture them fast, economically, and at scale.

It has been revealed that operations: Run large-scale global operations to collect the data. Volume alone is not enough; the data has to span every job in every industry.

Software and digital AI: Turn the raw output, which is far more voluminous and complex than text (e.g., multi-camera video, body and hand tracking, sensor streams), into high-quality, training-ready data.

Deployment: Put robots in front of end customers, for reinforcement learning and production deployment.

Each of these muscles is difficult to develop on its own, but to win, you need not one but all of them, working together and at scale. Training data today, for example, has to be high volume AND high diversity AND high quality AND delivered fast AND at a good price. It is easy to do one of these at small volume, but it is incredibly difficult to do all of them at once and at scale, and that is what it takes to help partners reach physical AGI. In the same way, it is easy to start a food delivery business that delivers a single dish from one restaurant to one apartment block, but it is incredibly difficult to scale it into a DoorDash.

Mecka's founders and team understood this and moved fast to build all five muscles, finding differentiated edge in each and executing on it. The result is a strong, scalable and flexible platform that has enabled them to win over many of the leading AI labs and robotics companies and quickly become the emerging leader of this category.

It has been revealed that what drew us to Mecka is not that they made the right bet on the right form of data (although they did). Robotics is still early relative to digital AI. The form factor of the data might change. The form factor of the robots might change. What matters is that they built the machine that scales with the industry and its partners; regardless of how the input changes over time, the output will be what their partners want. In the same way, DoorDash built a system where, whether the input is a pizza or a laptop, the customer gets the same delightful delivery experience. And when something in the physical world has high barriers to scale, it is an opportunity for the right team to build a large, durable business with moats.

That is why we are excited to back Josh, Jason and their fast-growing team. We see in them the special ingredients that will keep compounding over the long term to win this category and help their partners advance the mission of building and deploying robots at scale around the world.

And it is why others have joined us, from strategics like NVIDIA, Samsung, Microsoft and Qualcomm to the founders and operators who scaled some of the most defining companies of their generation and excel in many of the disciplines required in Meckaâs business: Tony Xu, founder and CEO of DoorDash; Frank Slootman, former CEO of ServiceNow and Snowflake; Milan Kovac, former head of Optimus at Tesla; Christopher Payne, former President & COO of Doordash; Jonathan Chadwick, former COO and CFO of VMware and board member at Databricks; and many more.Photo by S72 Business Portraits.

Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia’s offices on Monday to an applauding crowd of hundreds of employees, according to several videos circulating online.

The embattled Nvidia founder had stepped down earlier this month amid a series of scandals — including an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which has triggered multiple Congressional hearings over national security, and two affairs with Nvidia employees — but was reinstated as CEO after pushback from the tech community and an intervention by President Donald Trump.

After basking in chants of his name, Huang briefly addressed the crowd.

“Thank you all for the second chance,” he said. “I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around.”.

It has been revealed that over 200,000 people, including around 10,000 current Nvidia employees, had signed an open letter advocating for Huang’s return. Other tech leaders also pushed for Huang’s reinstatement, including Elon Musk, who noted last week at the DealBook Summit that letting Huang go is like “kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak.”.

Amid this increased scrutiny, however, other reports have depicted a different side to Nvidia’s top exec — one where Jensen is not seen as a beloved leader, but as a brutal bully. Based on decades of court documents and over a dozen interviews with current and former Nvidia employees, The New York Times reported that Huang “used humiliation as a tool” and verbally belittled staff at times.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, the company will be added to the Commerce Department’s Entity List, the outlet writes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Megaspeed, the manufacturer that Alice Huang — the woman at the center of the alleged Chinese espionage scandal involving Nvidia — led for over two years, will be placed on a U.S. Commerce Department blacklist, Semafor reported Monday.

According to recent reports, the company will be added to the Commerce Department’s Entity List, the outlet writes. This list “contains the names of foreign parties” subject to certain export restrictions designed to ensure that “sensitive technologies do not fall into the hands of those who would threaten U.S. national security or American citizens.”.

Functionally, what this will mean is that U.S. companies will not be able to do business with or sell products to Megaspeed without first gaining a special license from the federal government. Semafor cites anonymous sources familiar with the matter to note the move is designed to stop the organization “from obtaining US-made semiconductors.”.

Megaspeed is a Singapore-based cloud and AI infrastructure provider that, during the period that Nvidia’s boss, Jensen Huang, self-admittedly had an affair with Huang, was one of Nvidia’s biggest chip customers. Last week, the Commerce Department also unveiled it had rolled out a criminal probe into the company. Authorities in both the U.S. and Singapore are now probing whether the company defied export restrictions and illegally smuggled Nvidia chips to China. The company has denied wrongdoing.

TechCrunch reached out to the Commerce Department for comment on the reporting and will update this story if it responds.

After lobbying from President Trump, Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO on Monday after a short period in which he was ousted by the organization’s board over the scandal involving Huang.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A handful of tech CEOs, including Elon Musk, are celebrating Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia. Despite being caught in three affairs — including one with an alleged Chinese spy that has triggered multiple congressional investigations over national security concerns — Huang was reinstated as CEO and president of Nvidia on Monday morning.

“The mistake has been corrected,” Tesla and SpaceX leader Elon Musk wrote on X about Huang’s return.

The mistake has been corrected https://t.co/UKvEng9rCD.

Musk had been among the most vocal tech leaders to advocate for Huang.

“I think it’s like kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak, and it just doesn’t seem like a good thing for shareholders,” Musk said last week at the DealBook Summit.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman had taken a more neutral stance, commenting last week, “It’s hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen.”.

Altman had experienced a similar situation when he was ousted as CEO of OpenAI, then reinstated days later. After the announcement that Huang would return, Altman simply posted, “Jensen!” Many other tech CEOs have similarly refrained from commenting on the matter, given the shifting politics surrounding Huang’s ouster and reinstatement, as well as the national security concerns at the center of the controversy.

In addition to Musk, Binance co-founder and former CEO Changpeng Zhao (CZ), who served prison time for failing to stop criminal activity on the Binance crypto exchange, is also supportive of Huang.

“Glad to see @JensenHuang back,” CZ posted on X with a clapping hands emoji.

Glad to see @JensenHuang back. 👏 https://t.co/WrUjvmEyVi.

Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, who had been among 200,000 signatories on an open letter calling for Huang’s reinstatement, wrote on X, “Jensen’s return will be a demonstration of American resiliency to corporate, political and journalistic missteps.”.

Another signatory on the open letter, former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick, who had similarly been driven out of the firm he founded after scandals, also voiced his support for Huang on X.

Will have to save this for another day 😅😎 pic.twitter.com/dLqJosDpPZ.

When Nvidia’s stock tanked in reaction to Huang’s ousting, billionaire hedge fund manager Bill Ackman said he believes that the Nvidia board was “not acting in the best interest of shareholders nor in a manner consistent with their fiduciary duties.” As Nvidia’s stock began to rebound Monday morning, Ackman wrote, “The wisdom of the crowd prevails.”.

The attitude toward Huang’s return is not as celebratory outside of the tech industry. Across the political spectrum, some elected officials are skeptical about President Donald Trump’s claims that Huang’s return does not threaten national security.

In a recent development, “No national security risk? Based on what?” wrote Senator John Cornyn (R-TX).

Recent findings suggest that jensen Huang had multiple affairs including with subordinates and an alleged Chinese spy. His own board described his behavior as lacking “candor.” I’ve served on a public manufacturer board. His behavior does not support reinstatement.Nvidia’s decision today doesn’t excuse Jensen….

Senator Pete Ricketts (R-NB) added, “Nvidia’s decision today doesn’t excuse Jensen Huang from testifying before Congress. It also doesn’t absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips. I look forward to Mr. Huang coming to the Senate in December.”.

Huang is still expected to testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3, as well as privately before three House committees.

What if machine intelligence were as dependable as a database query?

What if machine intelligence were as dependable as a database query?

If models have reached superhuman intelligence, where is all the automation?

Industry observers note that the ChatGPT moment put AI front and center in the consumer mind. Claude Code transformed the life of the individual developer. With the âJev moment,â TypeSafe is going after the next paradigm: models that power software at runtime, making zillions of decisions with no humans in the loop.

Industry observers note that the early response has been extraordinary. Within 24 hours of launch on September 15, TypeSafeâs first model, Jev, became the fastest-adopted model in Vercelâs AI Gateway history. Over the past few weeks, weâve heard from many of our portfolio companies, who are racing to put it into production for a myriad of new use cases. It is the type of developer pull we havenât seen since GPT-3.

According to recent reports, jev flips the LLM on its head. Rather than writing out an answer word by word, it takes in context and a set of questions and returns typed answers with confidence scores, all at once. If LLMs are AIâs System 2, slow and deliberate, Jev is System 1: cheap, fast, intuitive and built for the thousands of small judgment calls software makes every second.

According to recent reports, thereâs so much you can do with Jev. Decide which button an agent should click next. Grade evals, route requests, triage tickets, pull fields out of contracts. Jev offers the kind of out-of-the-box generality that feels like magic, with no labeled data or training team required. Developers are finding newly introduced use cases every day, from playing Doom, to re-ranking their news feeds, to generating Super Mario multiverses.

Industry observers note that jev is named after Jevons paradox: when something gets dramatically cheaper, we use far more of it. TypeSafe is betting the same will be true of intelligence.

Sources indicate that when classification is expensive, teams ration it. They grade a sample of agent runs rather than all of them, define brittle rules instead of calling on a model, or ask one broad question instead of ten specific ones. When classification is nearly free, those tradeoffs go away.

That changes what is worth building. Many of the world's problems are Jev-shaped, which is obvious from the explosion of volume and creativity in use cases that folks are discovering. We think itâs likely that the most important things to be built on Jev havenât even been imagined yet.

Diogo Almeida first got the idea for TypeSafe while working on InstructGPT and RLHF at OpenAI. Models were being trained to be wonderful conversational partners â great for human interaction and human-in-the-loop. But, real automation needed something different: AI that is reliable, fast, and cheap. His conclusion, which he calls the âbitterest lesson,â was that picking the right task to solve matters even more than scale.

In a recent development, born in the Philippines and a *top 30* North American League of Legends player, Diogo is a rare mix: an iconoclastic, creative researcher with real developer taste and commercial instinct. He is wildly ambitious and refreshingly pragmatic, which is exactly what is needed to usher in the next machine age.

It has been revealed that jev has captured lightning in a bottle, but it is only the opening salvo. TypeSafe wants to become the infrastructure layer for how software makes decisions: a platform of primitives developers can compose and build on, the way they once built on databases.

We are absolutely thrilled to be partnering with Diogo, co-founders Sasha Sheng and Erik Spock Gafni, and the TypeSafe team in their Series A, behind our friends at a16z.

#26002. Supertake raises $20M to let AI agents turn your market predictions into stock portfolios

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1128 w)

AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 TechCrunch ↗ Open Full Page

Supertake raises $20M to let AI agents turn your market predictions into stock portfolios

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1128 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that AI investing startup Supertake has an interesting premise: What if your “takes” on the market could make you money without you having to pick stocks yourself?
  • According to recent reports, now, the tech giant has raised $20 million in seed funding to grow its business.
  • It has been revealed that michael Mignano originally incubated the startup at USV.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that AI investing startup Supertake has an interesting premise: What if your “takes” on the market could make you money without you having to pick stocks yourself? The service lets people turn their ideas into real investment portfolios, using frontier AI models and trading agents.

According to recent reports, now, the tech giant has raised $20 million in seed funding to grow its business. The round was led by venture firm Adjacent (Nico Wittenborn), with participation from Coinbase Ventures and Union Square Ventures (USV). Numerous angel investors also joined, including Nat Friedman, who’s at the moment head of product at Meta Superintelligence Labs; Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch; renowned product manager Nikita Bier; investor Scott Belsky; and Nemil Dalal, a former Coinbase exec who is now a visiting partner at Y Combinator.

It has been revealed that michael Mignano originally incubated the startup at USV. He is the co-founder and former CEO of the podcasting platform Anchor, which Spotify acquired in 2019 for over $150 million. After leading Spotify’s podcasting business as “Head of Talk” for a few years, he joined the team at Lightspeed as a venture partner, betting on AI companies like Suno and Granola. He also co-founded Oboe, an AI education startup, and joined USV as a general partner in April.

“We really believed there was an opportunity to make investing more democratized…and give everyone and anyone the ability to invest in their own insights and beliefs and ideas,” Mignano said. While he will continue in his role as founder and executive chairman, he’s now brought in a team to run the organization day to day.

The team includes co-founders Lincoln Murr (CEO) and John Peterson (CTO). Both joined from Coinbase, where, Mignano notes, they were the heads of AI product and engineering, leading introduces like Coinbase advisor, Coinbase for agents, agentic wallets, and others.

The startup arrives as AI continues to make inroads into financial services, but allowing AI to take over people’s actual investments requires a upcoming level of trust. Supertake is betting that people will ultimately be willing to take that leap, given recent improvements in frontier AI models.

Right now, Supertake works with Coinbase and Robinhood, and the company intends to expand to more brokerages over time. The idea is that you can explain, in broad, natural language, what you believe about how the world is going to change, and Supertake’s AI will iterate with you back and forth to turn that idea into a “take” that’s investable.

Under the hood, the startup is leveraging frontier AI technology and tools, combined with its own proprietary software that directs and limits what the AI can do.

Industry observers note that supertake’s customers’ ideas are tracked on a leaderboard on the site, so others who agree can invest alongside them. For instance, there’s currently an idea on the leaderboard about looksmaxxing and longevity becoming more of a trend, where the portfolio includes certain pharma and cosmetic companies that could potentially benefit.

For now, these portfolios consist of stock picks, but the team wants to expand the service over time to handle other types of transactions, like shorts, derivatives, perpetuals, long exposure, or even prediction markets — the latter handled through partnerships with companies in that space.

Despite these “takes” seeming like bets on what could happen next in a given market, Murr stresses that this doesn’t make Supertake itself a prediction market.

Industry observers note that “We think it’s a novel and very much improved way to create what was previously considered the robo-advisor experience,” he says. “When that came out, it had this amazing vision and direction of allowing people to have digital asset management. We think now is actually the time for that, with AI agents being so widely proliferated.”.

“I don’t think this is necessarily a prediction market by any means. The idea of natural language translation into an underlying set of assets feels different in that regard,” he says.

Still, the startup could wade into short-term predictions if a user’s take involves something they believe could happen in the near future, like who might win an election.

Recent findings suggest that “We’re primarily focused on the longer, medium-term holdings today. But that being stated, we don’t want to preclude people from building out very hyper short-term strategies that might exist,” Murr adds.

To address people’s concerns over AI managing their money, Supertake’s team says it’s implementing certain guardrails and spend limits. For instance, the AI has no ability to deposit or withdraw funds on a user’s behalf without their explicit consent. There are also drift limits in place so the portfolio stays balanced, plus allow and deny lists (meaning which assets the AI may and may not trade), real-time monitoring for anomalous activity, tools to set trade size limits, and a restriction that keeps agents from seeing the user’s brokerage credentials.

It has been revealed that “We view it as somewhat analogous to self-driving cars, actually, where there is a spectrum here of both trust and technological innovations that are happening,” says Murr. “Where a few years ago you may not feel comfortable getting in a car that has lane assist, but today you get in a Waymo, and it’s like nothing. And we think that there’s a very similar progression happening with the agentic finance space, and we’re far further along in the technological spectrum than people think.”.

Access to Supertake is still behind a waitlist while in beta, but the founders noted they’ve put their money where their mouths are. Murr and Peterson are letting it manage “tens of thousands” and “thousands” of dollars, respectively.

Mignano, meanwhile, says he has Supertake managing “hundreds of thousands” of dollars.

With the fresh funding, which follows a $2 million pre-seed round, Supertake aims to expand its team in areas like engineering, design, growth marketing, and others. Mignano and Murr are in New York, while Peterson is in the Austin area but commutes to New York at times. The team indicates it hopes to figure out a hybrid work model as it grows.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship. On Monday, the newly public AI company declared the launch of Claude Ship, a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes.

In a recent development, the latter is the more interesting part of this upcoming set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now. What’s notable about Claude Ship is not just that it can review proposed code changes and identify and address problems, but that it also includes an agent that can approve code changes automatically based on policies set by a development team.

The launch arrives at a time when AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving the code changes before they go live. With Claude Ship, the idea is to automate even more of the work involved in the development process, essentially by delegating approval authority to an AI agent itself.

Industry observers note that “Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” a organization blog post explains. “On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code, and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too.”.

Claude Ship is launching in beta, allowing early adopters to use it to review pull requests (PRs), and then decide what’s ready to merge.

Industry observers note that the new offering consists of Code Review, which is already generally available, and two new agents now in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. PR Steward focuses on addressing issues such as failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and feedback from Code Review. It also comments after every push on what it changed and how to roll it back, if needed.

In a recent development, claude Approvals then applies an approval policy that the team writes as a file in the repository. This approval process can incorporate various signals, including Code Review findings or the firm’s own classifiers, with policies written in natural language.

It has been revealed that because the offering is still in beta, Anthropic suggests running the approval functionality in observe-only mode first. Teams can also choose to start with just one repository and set monthly spending limits to have more control over the process.

Anthropic indicates teams will also still remain in control of where Claude Ship runs, which review settings to use (e.g., Quick, Standard, or Deep), and which changes should be escalated to a human for a decision.

Recent findings suggest that claude Ship is rolling out to Claude Team and Enterprise aims for repositories on GitHub. Code Review is generally available, while PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in beta.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 TechCrunch ↗ Open Full Page

Figma employee sues, alleging tech giant forced her to confront harassers

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1379 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Figma engineer is suing the design software manufacturer and its co-founder and CEO, Dylan Field, over allegations that she faced sexual harassment and retaliation while managers and HR repeatedly told her to confront the very people she accused of misconduct.
  • District Court for the Southern District of New York, alleges that Figma’s culture of “direct feedback” led managers and HR to make engineer Serry Park address harassment herself rather than investigate her complaints.
  • Recent findings suggest that “Figma was my dream tech giant for a long time,” Park told TechCrunch in an interview before the lawsuit was filed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Figma engineer is suing the design software manufacturer and its co-founder and CEO, Dylan Field, over allegations that she faced sexual harassment and retaliation while managers and HR repeatedly told her to confront the very people she accused of misconduct.

The lawsuit, filed Monday in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, alleges that Figma’s culture of “direct feedback” led managers and HR to make engineer Serry Park address harassment herself rather than investigate her complaints. Park, who joined Figma in 2022, alleges the organization’s response damaged her career, compensation, and mental health. The lawsuit also alleges that Park, who is Asian, faced racial and gender discrimination, including performance criticism based on stereotypes that Asian women are meek, timid, and conflict-averse.

Recent findings suggest that “Figma was my dream tech giant for a long time,” Park told TechCrunch in an interview before the lawsuit was filed. “It was a place where I felt that I could level up in my career, working on a lot of really cool, interesting things at scale.”.

Industry observers note that park is seeking damages, a jury trial, and a court order prohibiting Figma from requiring employees who report harassment to confront their alleged harassers. She also wants the company to adopt and enforce a process for investigating harassment complaints promptly and confidentially.

When reached for comment, a spokesperson for Figma remarked, “Figma does not tolerate discrimination or harassment. Figma also does not tolerate extortion. These claims have no merit, and we will present the facts in court.”.

According to recent reports, park told TechCrunch she initially had faith in Figma’s complaint process, expecting that if she documented the alleged harassment and reported it to the right people, the manufacturer would act. But as an engineer in a male-dominated field, Park told TechCrunch, “I don’t feel that they took me seriously throughout this process.”.

Park, who is still employed at Figma, joined its San Francisco office in October 2022. Within weeks, her onboarding mentor — a fellow engineer — asked her on a date and continued pursuing her after she declined, Park alleges. She initially feared reporting him, worrying that her manager would “dismiss her reports or view her as the problem,” according to the lawsuit.

Park says she tried to avoid her onboarding mentor. In early 2023, for example, she delayed choosing a work project until he had picked one. When her manager criticized her for not being a “team player,” Park explained that she was trying to avoid the colleague she accused of harassment, according to the suit.

Her manager allegedly dismissed her concerns, saying he had “met his wife at work too” and treating the behavior as “harmless flirtation.” When Park asked to be kept off projects with the onboarding mentor, HR allegedly instructed her to confront him directly about his behavior.

According to recent reports, the lawsuit ties that response to Figma’s culture of direct feedback, which Park alleges Field established and enforced. It indicates the tech giant’s People organization trains managers to direct employees, including those reporting harassment, to give feedback directly to the person involved.

In March 2023, her manager assigned him to a major project she was leading, despite her request to be separated from him. Park told her manager that she would “figure it out,” but alleges that having to work with him affected her performance. Her manager gave her a 2 out of 5 on her performance review, criticizing her for not speaking up enough or engaging with others and for lacking presence. Park was put on a coaching proposal, which she completed in late 2023.

It has been revealed that changing managers didn’t help, according to the lawsuit. Her second manager also refused to separate them, allegedly telling Park that someone at her level should be able to resolve conflicts with teammates and that separating them would be “avoiding the problem.” Like her previous manager, he allegedly pointed out that he had met his partner at work.

Park alleges the harassment continued throughout 2023.

In April 2024, she transferred to another team, a move she claims set back her career by resetting her performance and promotion timeline.

On her latest team, which had more women, Park said she felt better and no longer had to work with her alleged harasser. Her performance reviews improved, but in late 2025, she alleges another incident of sexual harassment, this time by her new manager.

According to recent reports, the incident followed a night out for drinks with her wife and two teammates, including her manager. The next day, during a team lunch, the manager allegedly said Park’s sex life had been discussed the previous evening. Park, who said no such conversation had occurred in her or her wife’s presence, felt “horrified and humiliated” by comments she believed fetishized queer relationships.

A colleague reported the comments to HR as sexual harassment, according to the suit. Weeks later, Park’s manager apologized in a Slack message, saying she didn’t recall what she had mentioned. When Park sought HR’s guidance, she was again told to address the matter directly with her manager.

During their conversation, the manager allegedly became defensive, and the encounter left Park feeling “crushed, anxious, and vulnerable.” The manager also allegedly noted she would never make such a comment because she had “a lot of gay friends.”.

Recent findings suggest that the manager told HR that they had agreed it was a misunderstanding. HR closed its investigation without interviewing witnesses, according to the suit, even though Park disputed her manager’s account.

“Requiring an employee to confront her harasser as the price of complaining — and then closing her complaint — would dissuade a reasonable employee from complaining at all,” the suit stated.

Park alleges her manager retaliated by publicly berating her, sometimes so aggressively that colleagues intervened or checked on her afterward, according to the lawsuit. The suit also alleges that other teammates left the team over concerns about the manager’s behavior.

Park again complained to HR about “escalating retaliation” and expressed concern the manager would “derail her career.” HR allegedly defended the manager’s conduct, saying the manager was “within her reasonable authority” and again instructed Park to address her concerns directly with the manager.

In early 2026, Park received another low performance review and a reduced bonus. The lawsuit alleges that similarly situated men continued to receive promotions, raises, and bonuses. When Park reported the negative performance review to HR in March, she was allegedly told her sexual harassment complaint against her manager could not be “substantiated.”.

Park took medical leave in March to receive treatment for PTSD symptoms and generalized anxiety. Cleared to return to work in June, she was prescribed workplace accommodations, including a graduated work schedule and mandatory remote workdays.

Park told TechCrunch that Figma approved the accommodations but had not implemented them at the time of the interview. In July, Park and her lawyers notified Figma of their intent to pursue legal action.

It has been revealed that “It’s really scary for me,” she said about taking legal action. “I don’t know what’s going to happen next with this, I don’t know what the outcome is going to be, but at least it feels like this is my chance to do the right thing.”.

Cresta began in 2017 out of the Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory. Zayd was the driving founder, bringing together a founding group that included Tim Shi, Sebastian Thrun, and Andre Esteva. Their thesis was simple, but contrarian for its time: build AI around people.

They wanted the same thing for knowledge work: the right answer at hand, the moment a rep needed it. Cresta was putting generative AI to work years before the category became mainstream.

Cresta emerged from stealth in 2020, just as businesses were shifting to remote work. Managers could no longer sit beside a fresh employee or coach across a contact center floor. They needed a way to train and support distributed teams. Crestaâs ability to deliver guidance in the moment became critical. Adoption accelerated. Product-market fit was taking hold.

From proving the product to scaling the company.

Many of those early engineers remain at Cresta today, carrying forward years of technical knowledge and customer understanding. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • AI agents will ask far more questions of a manufacturer's data than people ever did.
  • Recent findings suggest that AI agents will ask far more questions of a company's data than people ever did.
  • Sources indicate that last fall we got a message from Roy Reznik, one of the co-founders of Wiz, offering to introduce us to a team that had just left Microsoft.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI agents will ask far more questions of a manufacturer's data than people ever did. Edelbyte is building the data platform that can answer all of them, fast and at a price that makes sense.

Recent findings suggest that AI agents will ask far more questions of a company's data than people ever did. Edelbyte is building the data platform that can answer all of them, fast and at a price that makes sense.

Sources indicate that last fall we got a message from Roy Reznik, one of the co-founders of Wiz, offering to introduce us to a team that had just left Microsoft. This was the only introduction to a founding team weâd ever received from Roy, and we paid attention.

Sources indicate that the people Roy wanted us to meet had built Kusto, a data engine that started more than a decade ago as a small incubation project inside Microsoft. Named after the oceanographer Jacques Cousteau because it was built for diving into oceans of data, Kusto was designed to get answers from enormous volumes of fast-arriving data, such as logs, telemetry and security events, in seconds rather than hours. It ran on a query language simple enough that anyone, not just substantial-data engineers, could use it. And it worked so well that it became the data engine underneath Microsoft Sentinel, Microsoft Defender and Azure Monitor, and was eventually offered to customers as Azure Data Explorer. Security teams in particular loved it, which is how Roy became one of its biggest champions. When we spoke with customers, large enterprises and fast-growing startups alike told us two things: it was game-changing data technology, and the team behind it was among the best theyâd ever worked with.

Recent findings suggest that avner Aharoni, Evgeney Ryzhyk, Alexander Sloutsky and Yoni Leibowitz were that team. Evgeney invented the Kusto engine and its query language, then rebuilt it three times, making it faster and cheaper with each iteration. Alexander turned half-formed ideas into finished features seemingly overnight, and Yoni made sure every complex design was fully thought through, starting before a line of code was ever written. Avner, who spent a quarter century at Microsoft, hustled Kusto from project to a globally beloved product. Their new tech giant, Edelbyte, builds on this success. We are proud to have led their seed round and to be their partners.

According to recent reports, in B2B technology, this is a proven playbook: a team develops a solution inside a large manufacturer and then splits off to build it independently. Itâs the origin story of Sequoia portfolio companies such as Confluent, whose founders created Kafka at LinkedIn, and Temporal, whose founders built Cadence at Uber. Edelbyte now follows the same path.

But Edelbyte is not simply Kusto rebuilt for a fourth time; it is a rethinking, from first principles, of what a data platform should look like in the age of AI. With every major shift in computing, the way software is built changes, and the data infrastructure underneath it has to change too. Data platforms were designed around human people, and there is a natural limit on the number of questions one person can type in a day. That made the trade-offs, such as keeping less history so queries stay fast, asking fewer questions so the bill stays reasonable, and building the product inside whichever cloud the database happens to run in, easier to tolerate.

It has been revealed that but an AI agent investigating a problem is like a whole team of curious analysts who never get tired, testing multiple hypotheses concurrently. One agent might fire off fifty queries where a person would run one. And at that scale, rationing and trade-offs rapidly constrain the true promise of AI. An agent is only as useful as the questions it can afford to ask, and what it can afford is decided in the data layer.

According to recent reports, edelbyte keeps detailed history queryable at interactive speed, scales as data volumes and query demand grow, and gives people, applications and AI agents governed access to the same data. It brings search and analytics, which have historically been stitched together from separate systems at significant cost and complexity, together in a single platform. And it runs wherever you need it: in the cloud or on premises, managed or self-hosted.

The result is exactly what an AI-heavy workload needs: no more rationing curiosity, whether it comes from a person or an agent. Already, customers are seeing dramatic increases in efficiency, including tenfold increases in queries with no increase in budget.

It has been revealed that data platforms are among the most durable and lucrative businesses in technology, because data has gravity; once it accumulates in one place it rarely moves. Each era produces its own winners, and we believe the AI era will be won by the platform that lets builders, and the agents working for them, ask as many questions as they want without worrying about the speed or the bill. Edelbyte is building just such a platform, and we are thrilled to be part of the journey.

#25968. Industry News: Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI model training – here’s how

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (508 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Zdnet ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI model training – here’s how

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (508 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google likes to use your conversations with Gemini for model training to help improve the AI.
  • Also: I checked Gemini’s newly introduced Memory summary to see what it knew about me.
  • Recent findings suggest that in a change set to roll out in the coming weeks, you’ll be able to put the brakes on Gemini model training without losing access to your previous conversations with the AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google likes to use your conversations with Gemini for model training to help improve the AI. But for people with privacy concerns, the only way to opt out of this was to delete your entire chat history. Now, Google is overhauling the process to eliminate that drawback.

Also: I checked Gemini’s newly introduced Memory summary to see what it knew about me.

Recent findings suggest that in a change set to roll out in the coming weeks, you’ll be able to put the brakes on Gemini model training without losing access to your previous conversations with the AI. Here’s how this works now — and how it will work down the road.

Presently, Gemini offers a setting called Keep Activity that controls not only whether and for how long your chats are saved but also whether they’re used to train the AI. You can’t separate the two.

To correct this problem, Google will replace Keep Activity with two upcoming settings. With the first setting, you’ll be able to keep or delete your past chats and choose how long your history will be saved. With the second setting, you’ll be able to decide whether your chats, including all text and attachments, will be used for model training.

Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes.

“With this change, you will be able to keep your history while independently controlling generative AI model training,” Google stated in an announcement shared to Gemini users via email.

According to recent reports, here’s how this will play out. If your Keep Activity setting is off when this change is made, both fresh settings will be off. If your Keep Activity setting is on, both new settings will be on. That means you’ll need to head to Gemini’s Settings if you wish to opt out of model training but still be able to view and access your previous chats.

Almost all AIs include a setting for model training that you typically have to manually disable if you’re concerned about your privacy. But most let you opt out without turning off your chat history.

ChatGPT offers a setting called “Improve the model for everyone,” which is double-speak for model training. But this is easy enough to turn off. Microsoft Copilot provides settings for “Training on conversation activity” and “Training on voice conversations,” both of which you can disable to opt out of model training. Claude’s AI training option is turned off by default. But you can always control this by checking the setting for “Help improve our AI models.”.

Also: 5 ways AI will change how you defend your business in 2027.

In all those cases, you still retain access to your conversation history. In contrast, Google has been the only AI player among the majors to impose a restriction for those who want to opt out of AI training. Based on past actions, Google has often earned a reputation for being privacy-unfriendly. I’m glad to see the manufacturer take this step in the right direction.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • While the first Googlebooks on the market have received mixed reviews, these features could help the laptops gain more useful features in Chrome that other browsers already offer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Monday, Google rolled out an M157 enhancement for the Chrome web browser on Googlebook OS, with a handful of fresh features and performance boosts to streamline your workflow and browsing experience.

While the first Googlebooks on the market have received mixed reviews, these features could help the laptops gain more useful features in Chrome that other browsers already offer.

In a recent development, also: Googlebooks? The best laptop for Android users is something else.

Here are the five latest Chrome features on Googlebook OS to know about.

If you’ve ever had to share your screen on a video call, you know how irritating it can be to switch tabs without having to repeatedly start and stop sharing. This Chrome upgrade adds a tab-sharing controls bar; when you share a browser tab in a video call, Chrome will display a persistent control bar at the top of the window so you can “Stop sharing” or “Share this tab instead” from any tab.

Also: 6 Chrome default settings I changed to instantly.

When you hover over a collapsed vertical tab rail with your mouse or trackpad, it will expand, so you can read full tab titles, switch tabs, or manage groups. The rail will collapse again when you move the cursor away.

Recent findings suggest that this auto-expand feature is enabled by default. If you want to turn it off or on, go to Settings > Appearance > Tab position > “Auto expand tabs on hover,” or right-click the vertical tab rail.

Industry observers note that the Chrome patch allows you to manually resize your vertical tab bar to view longer page titles when needed. The browser will remember your custom tab width, even after you open a new window or restart the browser. (You’ll just need to turn “Auto expand tabs on hover” off for it to work.).

You can now save individual Chrome Settings subpages as direct web addresses that you can type, bookmark, or link to directly (for example, chrome://settings/privacy), meaning you won’t have to go digging around in menus to change your preferences anymore. You can navigate between these Settings subpages with the Back and Forward buttons.

The system’s “Save As” file picker is now enabled by default for menu save actions, such as “Save link as” and “Save image as,” so you can more easily rename files and select a destination folder. This includes Google Drive or external storage.

In a recent development, also: Google Chrome running slow? 5 easy ways to speed it up fast.

Outside of these new features, a few of Chrome M157’s performance fixes include the ability to press Ctrl+L to reveal and select web addresses; keeping your bookmarks bar visible in fullscreen mode and while screen sharing; better media controls while using Picture-in-Picture mode; and the ability to partially translate PDFs within your browser.

If you have Chrome set up to automatically download and install updates, you won’t have to lift a finger to take advantage of the upcoming features and performance boosts.

But if you’ve disabled automatic updates, you can manually update by selecting the three-dot menu in the top-right corner of your Chrome window and navigating to Help > About Google Chrome > Relaunch.

Also: My week with upcoming Googlebooks: The good, the bad, and the promising.

If the Relaunch option is greyed out or nowhere to be found, you’re running on the latest version of Chrome. And if you were working on something before the enhancement, don’t worry: Chrome will save your open tabs and reopen them automatically when you restart.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that google is replacing Gemini Gems with Skills starting Nov. 17, 2026, and it’s carrying over features that let you share Skills and add files from Google products.

Sources indicate that google has confirmed that it’s turning Gems, a Gemini feature that lets you create customizable AI chatbots, into Skills, which let you create custom instructions for Gemini. Any Gems you have created will automatically convert, but you can transfer them manually if you want to start using them now.

To help with the transition, Google revealed that two Gems features are moving, too: the ability to share creations and to include Drive, Notebook, and Photos files as part of your Skill’s instructions.

While the Gemini Gems feature is technically going away, any Gems you’ve created aren’t.

If you access the Gems portion of Gemini (since the feature is on the way out, you now have to access this through Settings), you’ll see a message that indicates “Starting November 17, 2026, we’ll automatically begin migrating all of your Gems to Skills.” (The cutoff date for accessing your Gems will be Dec. 16, 2026. Workspace business, enterprise, and non-profit accounts will get cut off in March 2027, and Workspace education accounts will be cut off in June 2027.).

In a recent development, A Gemini Skill functions much the same as a Gem. You describe specific situations when Gemini should use the Skill automatically and tell Gemini what you want the Skill to do (it’s best to give specific examples of output). Google gives the example of a marketing team sharing a brand-voice skill that references their brand guidelines doc in Drive, or a team lead sharing an onboarding skill based on the team handbook.

The biggest difference is that Gems were standalone chats, while Skills are custom instructions that work in any conversation.

You can create as many Skills as you want, but only 100 can be active at a time.

To get users familiar with Skills, Google is bringing over two features from Gems.

First, you can now share any Skill with other owners. When you share a Skill, you can choose whether the other person has permission to edit or view only. To share a Skill, go to the three-bar menu in the top left > Customize > Skills. You can view or change permissions from that screen.

Also: I checked Gemini’s latest Memory summary to see what it knew about me – how to see and edit yours.

When a Skill is added, Gemini can use it automatically, or you can @mention it in chat to trigger it. One small caveat, though: you can only share Skills through the Gemini web app at the moment, not the mobile app.

Industry observers note that additionally, when you’re creating a Gemini Skill, you can choose to include files of up to 100MB from other Google products like Drive, Photos, and Notebook, along with files from your local device. Gemini will reference these files every time the Skill runs and update in real time, Google says. These features existed with Gems; Google is just moving them to Skills to make the new feature more comparable.
