📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Drone and missile strikes have inflicted unprecedented damage on data centers in Eastern Europe and the Middle East this year, disrupting cloud services for millions of people and permanently deleting some Amazon Web Services customer data. This trend represents a new concern for Massive Tech companies—but also for governments and everyone else who depends on common digital services in modern life.

To explore what this all means for modern society’s reliance on cloud resilience, I will be hosting a live conversation titled “Drone attacks and data centers: Latest Risks for Massive Tech” on Tuesday, November 17 at 1 pm ET with Joseph Jarnecki, a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), a UK defense and security think tank. He leads RUSI’s work on how cloud services factor into national security and defense, along with tech sovereignty efforts.

Jarnecki has done extensive research on how Ukraine strengthened its cloud resilience with Western partners despite facing both cyberattacks and kinetic attacks at the start of the full-scale Russian invasion, and explored what that means for NATO and European governments’ cloud adoption plans.

This year, Jarnecki has written about Iran’s drone and missile strikes on Amazon data centers in the Middle East during the US-Israeli war with Iran, and the broader implications for governments and Substantial Tech. He has also commented on the impacts of Russia and Ukraine exchanging strikes on each other’s data centers.

For more background on the data center attacks that have transpired so far in 2026, you can see my previous Ars coverage of how the Iranian strikes left Amazon with months of repairs, and caused enough damage to result in the permanent loss of some AWS customer data.

I’ve also covered why Russia was not ready for the data center war it started with Ukraine, with the systematic Russian strike campaign targeting Ukraine’s data centers provoking Ukrainian counterstrikes that damaged Russian government data centers and AI data centers owned by the Russian tech giant Yandex.

My conversation with Jarnecki will explore why data centers have become much more prominent military targets, whether defending or hardening data centers against drones and missiles is a realistic option, how cloud resiliency can be improved in wartime conditions, and the choices governments and cloud providers face in deploying data centers during an era of growing geopolitical risks.

You can watch the discussion live on YouTube on November 17 at 1 pm ET. We will also be fielding a few audience questions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that you don’t need to buy a gaming headset to play GTA VI on your PS5 or Xbox Series X|S. You can use headphones you already own by connecting them to your controller with a compatible audio cable and adjusting a few settings.

It’s been a long 13-year wait for GTA VI, but with the holiday gift-buying season so close, you may be strapped for cash to buy a gaming headset, especially after spending $80 to $100 on the game. The good thing is that GTA VI is strictly single-player right now, so you don’t need a headset with a mic to enjoy it. You can also easily turn a pair of headphones you already have into a makeshift gaming headset.

It has been revealed that also: Can your PC run GTA VI? Minimum requirements to expect.

Sources indicate that however, since your consumer headphones aren’t primed for console gaming, you’ll need to tweak some audio settings. Here’s what you need to know.

Whether playing on a PS5 or an Xbox Series X|S, you’ll need to wire your headphones to your controller. Neither console supports standard Bluetooth audio.

Your everyday consumer headphones have a different sound profile than gaming headphones.

Sources indicate that gaming headphones tend to offer clearer directional cues, so you can hear an enemy’s footsteps approaching. Consumer headphones are generally more bass-heavy, which can mask more intricate sounds of faraway dialogue, footsteps, or ambient sounds.

With a bass-boosted EQ, the low end of explosions, gunshots, and crashes may be too intense, and less prominent highs could make it harder to hear vital cues like car doors full of a vengeful gang shutting, an NPC asking for a favor in the distance, or a scorned Leonidan whispering your location.

Also: Fake GTA 6 PC downloads are flooding the web.

If you’re adamant about going wireless with your everyday headphones, you might try to use a Bluetooth dongle or a workaround with your TV. If you must use a dongle, it should support the same codecs as your headphones. If there’s a mismatch, the devices may default to the lower-quality SBC codec, potentially delivering poorer sound and higher latency.

Sources indicate that if you connect your console to your TV and wirelessly connect your headphones to your TV, you may get a significant lag between your in-game actions and the audio in your headphones. I don’t recommend this either.

Also: How to play retro console games on modern systems: 3 ways.

It has been revealed that I also don’t recommend using high-impedance studio headphones, as your controller may not have enough power to drive them adequately. Finally, I don’t recommend using your headphones’ built-in spatial audio rendering at all, especially when it’s on top of your console’s rendering. Double spatial audio rendering can make your audio sound strange, and you may lose the directional cues spatial audio is supposed to enhance.

If you want spatial audio, configure these settings in your console’s audio settings.

Using your everyday headphones with your gaming console isn’t a long-term solution, but it can work in a pinch, especially if you want to play late into the night without disturbing your housemates. With some tweaking to your headphones’ and console’s audio settings, you can make it work, but before GTA VI Online comes out, put a solid pair of gaming headphones on your holiday wish list.

AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

Google makes it easier to use Gemini without training AI on your data

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (551 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It can be hard to use Google products—or even the Internet itself—without coming into contact with Gemini AI.
  • In a recent development, the change presently rolling out to Gemini will separate your chat history from training, which allows you to retain basic AI functionality without handing Google quite so much control over your data.
  • As the new settings roll out, owners will see separate toggles for model training and chat history.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It can be hard to use Google products—or even the Internet itself—without coming into contact with Gemini AI. That is, of course, by design. The more you use Gemini, the more data Google collects to train and improve its generative AI chatbot. The options to limit training on your data have been scant, but Google is finally adding more controls to the Gemini app.

In a recent development, the change presently rolling out to Gemini will separate your chat history from training, which allows you to retain basic AI functionality without handing Google quite so much control over your data. Prior to this change, the only way to opt out of contributing your chat contents (including attachments) for training was to turn off your history. That made it impossible to go back and pick up a chat down the road.

As the new settings roll out, owners will see separate toggles for model training and chat history. The history setting will continue to support an adjustable limit, but you will no longer have to change it to stop Google from training on your Gemini usage. Meanwhile, AI training will be an opt-out situation. You’ll need to find the toggle to block Google from using your chats for AI training. It’s under Activity in the Gemini settings. You can also access the menu from your Google account under Data and Privacy > My Activity > Other activity > Gemini Apps Activity.

Importantly, this only applies to future interactions with Gemini. If you have previously fed any data into Google’s AI, that’s already part of the training data. That can include your inputs, Gemini’s responses, uploaded files, tool calls, your location, and data from connected apps. Google says it may retain this data for up to three years to improve its models. The firm has previously noted it attempts to filter personal information out of the Gemini activity history, but that isn’t a guarantee.

Industry observers note that regardless of your chosen activity settings, you can always manually remove anything you don’t want saved on the same page with the history and training toggles. However, reviewed chats that are already part of the training data won’t be retroactively deleted. Opting out of training doesn’t mean Google won’t have your data, either. Google may use this data in other ways for up to three years—it just won’t add it to AI-training data sets.

Recent findings suggest that if you want to use Gemini and not retain any data, your options are actually a bit more limited now. Right now, if you disable history, Google still retains that data for 72 hours (and 24 hours for the user). Once the updated page is live, this duration will change to two months. So you can access that data for longer, but so can Google. The company claims this is to “respond to you, process your feedback, and protect Google, its owners, and the public.” Essentially, Google will be more able to identify nefarious AI usage even if someone disables history.

Industry observers note that even with the longer chat retention, the ability to control AI training is still a welcome privacy improvement. Google indicates the change is rolling out globally, but it may take a few weeks to show up for everyone.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • On Monday, large trucks began circling the streets of Washington, DC, carrying billboards urging Congress to investigate the Trump administration’s ties with Nvidia’s disgraced CEO Jensen Huang.
  • “Jensen was in bed with a spy from China,” the billboards created by the Tech Oversight Project (TOP) alleged.
  • Presently, Trump is supporting a campaign to bring back Huang as Nvidia’s CEO—despite many Republicans calling it a “horrible idea.” Breaking his silence, Huang issued a statement Tuesday saying he would be “honored” to return, but the board remarked reinstatement is not under consideration as an internal investigation into US spying claims remains ongoing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Monday, large trucks began circling the streets of Washington, DC, carrying billboards urging Congress to investigate the Trump administration’s ties with Nvidia’s disgraced CEO Jensen Huang.

“Jensen was in bed with a spy from China,” the billboards created by the Tech Oversight Project (TOP) alleged. “Trump was in bed with Jensen.” TOP is a nonprofit that describes itself as “dedicated to reining in Big Tech.”.

Presently, Trump is supporting a campaign to bring back Huang as Nvidia’s CEO—despite many Republicans calling it a “horrible idea.” Breaking his silence, Huang issued a statement Tuesday saying he would be “honored” to return, but the board remarked reinstatement is not under consideration as an internal investigation into US spying claims remains ongoing. Huang used the moment to say that his interests align with the US’s, saying:.

I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. Nvidia has been my life’s work. Building it into the tech giant it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like Nvidia be possible. I love our country, and I love Nvidia.

Trump may have learned as early as this spring that Huang was potentially the target of Chinese espionage, but the president claimed recently that he didn’t know Huang was potentially exposed to a Chinese spy as he was becoming a prominent part of Trump’s inner circle, CNN reported.

If Trump wasn’t adequately briefed, it raises question about whether the White House acted with “sufficient urgency” to address a serious espionage threat, CNN said. But if Trump is deflecting, an even “graver question” will emerge about why Trump didn’t act on information and instead continued to keep Huang close, CNN said.

Instead of distancing himself from the Nvidia CEO, Trump invited Huang to sit at the head table during a state dinner with China’s president Xi Jinping, and last month, Trump awarded Huang the National Medal of Science, the nation’s highest scientiﬁc honor, for his AI achievements.

“Not only has he continued to do nothing, he’s invited that very CEO into the White House and on state visits to China with him,” Sacha Haworth, TOP’s founder and CEO, told Ars. “And the question we all have to ask is ‘why on Earth would he do that?’”.

It has been revealed that what Trump and Nvidia knew—and when—have become central questions for some Republicans, as well as top Democrats who initiative to investigate the scandal when they assume control of key committees in Congress next year. Andrew Yoon, head of research for a nonprofit called CivAI, which warns the public of dangers from AI, told Ars that Huang doesn’t need to be compromised by China to have endangered the US. Prioritizing boosting profits over national security alone is “pretty concerning.”.

“I think the most notable thing here is that Jensen Huang has been at the absolute forefront of lobbying to be able to sell chips to China,” Yoon noted. “He has leveraged his very deep relationships with government, especially President Trump, in order to be able to sell as many Nvidia chips to China as he can get away with. If he could be selling Blackwell chips to China, I’m sure he would be.”.

Yoon noted that evidence suggests some Chinese AI models have been trained on Blackwell chips. Even with China’s push to prioritize domestic chipmakers like Huawei, Nvidia chips remain “indispensable” to China’s frontier AI goals, Yoon noted. And national security experts fear that access to high-end chips will help China advance its military AI or gain economic ground.

The White House isn’t commenting on Trump’s relationship with Huang. Among the lawmakers accusing the Trump administration of “corruption” is Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), The Wall Street Journal reported. He has already asked the White House to “preserve all communications” between Trump and Huang.

It has been revealed that other lawmakers are “seeking more information about what Trump knew about the relationship between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang,” the former Megaspeed CEO whom Huang admitted to having an affair with. They also want to know more about “the administration’s failure to stop artiﬁcial-intelligence chips from going to China,” WSJ reported, and Nvidia’s reportedly $25 million donation to the White House ballroom.

“It is not just an intelligence concern; it’s also a potential corruption issue,” Blumenthal said. “There needs to be a really penetrating, comprehensive investigation of all the possible compromises of our intelligence that may have occurred, but also… that Donald Trump is so high on the head of Nvidia, and now is potentially linked to intelligence compromises.”.

Industry observers note that trump has profited off Nvidia’s success while in office, buying “millions of dollars worth of Nvidia shares in his personal brokerage accounts since returning to oﬃce in 2025,” the WSJ reported. The White House maintains that the president has no role in managing his stock portfolio.

Other officials advising Trump on AI also benefited from relaxing export curbs, TOP remarked. On Tuesday, the group issued a report summarizing what the public knows about potential conflicts of interest of two Trump officials: former White House AI Czar David Sacks and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.

Haworth, TOP’s founder, told Ars she’s concerned that Sacks and Lutnick abused their power to convince Trump to let Nvidia sell cutting-edge technology to China, while standing to “gain astronomical amounts of money.”.

It has been revealed that “The public is outraged by Nvidia’s CEO for compromising our national security, but we didn’t get here because of Jensen Huang’s missteps alone,” Haworth said. If “Nvidia was knowingly doing business with companies tied to illegal chip sales and smuggling with China,” then “the Trump administration was asleep at the wheel,” she said.

“White House AI Czar David Sacks and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick were protecting their own fortunes rather than looking out for Americans,” Haworth remarked.

If the US fails to hold them accountable for alleged conflicts of interest, “it would send a signal that powerful men once again cannot be held to account and that powerful men are protecting powerful men,” Haworth said.

According to recent reports, detailing Sacks’ alleged conflicts, the group cited Upcoming York Times reporting that the former AI czar had long supported Huang’s stance that allowing Nvidia to sell more chips in China would help the US stay ahead in the AI race. After Sacks became Trump’s key AI advisor, Huang rapidly forged a “tight bond” with him, and “both stood to benefit” from their push to sell chips to China, TOP reported.

According to recent reports, also notably, while advising the White House, Sacks opposed policies such as the Trump administration’s recent move to cut off China’s remote access to US-made chips through now-restricted Southeast Asian data centers. Citing Sacks’ alignment with Huang, TOP reported that after just one meeting with the two men, Trump decided to allow Nvidia to sell AI chips to China that the Biden administration had previously blocked.

Huang valued his alliance with Sacks, TOP noted, citing reporting that showed Huang declaring last year that Nvidia was “lucky” to have Sacks advising Trump. But TOP is concerned that the alliance was built on mutual financial interest and that Sacks took a part-time role in the Trump administration to avoid divestments or disclosure requirements that might have revealed the extent of his possible conflicts of interest.

TOP flagged two areas it believes warrant Congressional investigation. While advising Trump to embrace AI deregulation, Sacks and his firm, Craft Ventures, continued investing substantially in AI. Sacks also stood to benefit from pushing Trump to integrate AI into warfare and national security tools, TOP’s report stated. Craft Ventures has invested in Palantir, “a Peter Thiel-founded government contractor seen as a ‘rising star’ in the US Defense Tech World and holding hundreds of millions in US government defense contracts,” TOP said.

Even within the Trump administration, officials have turned on Commerce Secretary Lutnick, seemingly looking to blame him for mishandling the Nvidia spying investigation and allowing Trump to maintain close ties with Huang despite apparent intelligence risks.

In a recent development, lutnick has bragged publicly that he promised Huang “really easy access to the President” after joining the administration, TOP reported. That alliance helped push Trump to approve the sale of Nvidia H200s to China, TOP noted. And that seemed to directly benefit Lutnick, TOP said, because before he was confirmed as secretary, he was CEO of Cantor Fitzgerald, which held $1.2 billion in Nvidia stock.

Sources indicate that “In his role as Secretary, Lutnick is responsible for policing exports of sensitive technology to adversaries and global rivals, like China,” TOP reported. “Lutnick and the company he controls benefited greatly from opening sales of Nvidia chips to China.”.

After Lutnick was required to hand that organization over to his son, Cantor Fitzgerald “maintained extensive commercial ties to Nvidia, helping arrange billions of dollars in financing for companies in its AI business universe and repeatedly hosting its top executives,” TOP noted.

According to recent reports, those investments shifted substantially around the same time that Lutnick began facing pressure to “crack down on Megaspeed, a Singapore-based manufacturer suspected of funneling Nvidia’s advanced artificial intelligence chips to China,” TOP reported. Cantor Fitzgerald “reduced its Nvidia holdings by nearly 50 percent between September 2025 and March 2026,” TOP said.

Sources indicate that however, when Trump was reportedly first told of the spying allegations this spring, Cantor Fitzgerald again continued to boost Nvidia. Most prominently, the manufacturer helped “finance the expansion of one of Nvidia’s newest business partners, IREN,” facilitating a five-year, $3.4 billion deal between Nvidia and the Australia-based cloud computing provider.

Recent findings suggest that among those now criticizing Lutnick for weak enforcement of export controls that appeared designed to protect Huang’s bottom line is Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. But even with scrutiny coming from within the Trump administration, not everyone is convinced that Lutnick did anything wrong. Yoon suggested that, given Lutnick’s long career, there may be normal explanations for potential financial conflicts.

“Maybe a separate question is ‘should people with a long storied history in business and industry be working in government at this level?’” Yoon noted.

Haworth stated the next 48 hours will be critical in determining whether Huang succeeds in returning to Nvidia.

“I think it’s going to be incumbent on the incoming Democratic leadership to insist that whether or not he returns, investigations will follow,” Haworth said.

But Yoon thinks Nvidia is unlikely to bring Huang back any time soon, despite current evidence suggesting that “Nvidia’s actions here have been perfectly legal” and that “influencing a political system for your financial interests is very much legal in the United States.”.

It seems “untenable for Nvidia to continue doing what they’re doing,” Yoon said. Zooming out even more, he suggested the scandal showed that the entire AI industry can no longer afford to operate under a profit motive alone, so long as governments continue positioning the technology as a strategic asset.

Sources indicate that if US investigations expose corruption, bribery, treason, or other crimes, Nvidia risks losing some of its dominant stake in the GPU market. On Tuesday, The Information reported that some Nvidia customers had already lost trust and were looking to Google and AMD for more stability.

Nvidia has also been accused of intervening in a Commerce investigation, which Yoon noted could also be “pretty consequential” if any evidence bears that out.

Industry observers note that “I think it’s pretty unlikely that Huang makes it back to Nvidia any time soon,” Yoon said. “Maybe he goes on a redemption tour and comes back in five years or something, but I’m not really seeing a path forward for him right now.”.

Perps and Swaps: How to Trade the News on Decrypt

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that readers have traditionally learned about markets in one place and traded them in another.
  • Decrypt set out to close that gap in September 2026, when it confirmed The Information Exchange: a network that brings together news, data, market prices, probabilities and the ability to trade, around the subjects readers follow.
  • The Information Exchange sees Decrypt delivering both the reporting and the market infrastructure that links information to trading, while the Solana blockchain provides the network on which trades settle, including token swaps and perpetual futures.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that readers have traditionally learned about markets in one place and traded them in another. A story about Bitcoin, a public manufacturer or a commodity might shape a view, but acting on it meant opening an exchange or a trading app and starting over.

Decrypt set out to close that gap in September 2026, when it confirmed The Information Exchange: a network that brings together news, data, market prices, probabilities and the ability to trade, around the subjects readers follow.

The Information Exchange sees Decrypt delivering both the reporting and the market infrastructure that links information to trading, while the Solana blockchain provides the network on which trades settle, including token swaps and perpetual futures.

This guide explains what each one is and how to trade it on Decrypt.

Everything on The Information Exchange runs through a Decrypt Money Account, which rolled out on Solana in October 2026.

Sources indicate that A Money Account holds one balance that funds every product on Decrypt: swaps, perpetual futures and prediction markets.The account is self-custodial, meaning Decrypt does not hold customers' private keys and cannot act on their behalf. It is designed to work without seed phrases, and network fees are covered, so users don't need to hold SOL, Solana's native token, to pay for transactions.

In a recent development, in November 2026, Decrypt added confidential transfers, using Solana Privacy Rings from infrastructure firm Helius. Users can send funds without the amounts appearing on Solana's public ledger, and can switch the feature on by selecting "Enable" on the Private Balance panel of the Portfolio page. As of November 2026, privacy applies to transfers only, not to swaps or prediction market positions.

Solana Privacy Rings use zero-knowledge proofs, which let consumers prove they own and can spend a balance without revealing how much it holds.

It has been revealed that A swap exchanges one token for another at the current market price. Instead of placing an order on an exchange and waiting for it to fill, the trader sends one token and receives another in a single transaction.

Swaps on Decrypt are powered by Jupiter, a Solana trading platform that offers swaps, lending, borrowing, perpetual futures and portfolio tools. Jupiter finds prices across Solana's trading venues, so owners don't need to choose where a trade is executed.

At time of publication, swaps cover a select group of major cryptocurrencies and Solana tokens, as well as tokenized stocks, commodities and other real-world assets.

As of November 2026, the Assets panel of the Portfolio page groups holdings into crypto, stocks, commodities and collectibles, and lists tokens including SOL, BTC, ETH, XRP and HYPE.

Perpetual futures, or perps, are contracts that let traders bet on whether an asset's price will rise or fall without owning the asset. Unlike traditional futures, they have no expiry date. A trader who expects the price to rise goes "long," and one who expects it to fall goes "short.".

Perps are usually traded with leverage, which lets a trader control a larger position than their deposit would otherwise allow. Leverage magnifies gains and losses alike, and if the market moves against a position far enough, it can be liquidated, or closed automatically, wiping out the trader's margin.

Perps on Decrypt are powered by Phoenix, a fully onchain perpetuals exchange on Solana developed by Ellipsis Labs—making Decrypt the first media platform to offer perps trading alongside its journalism.

CISA Adds Four Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog mlove Nov 20, 2026 Release DateNovember 20, 2026 DescriptionCISA has added four new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation.CVE-2025-42884 SAP NetWeaver Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic VulnerabilityCVE-2026-76466 Cisco Expressway Series Use of Hard-coded Credentials VulnerabilityCVE-2026-123890 VMWare vCenter Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel VulnerabilityCVE-2026-129448 Apache Roller Deserialization of Untrusted Data VulnerabilityThese types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise. Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities. CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria. Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form. Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance. Breaking: Copilot is "the upcoming OS for work," and now Office runs inside of it

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Opening the keynote at its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the manufacturer’s vision for its fresh “frontier ecosystem,” announcing Tuesday the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he described as “the new OS for work.”.
  • According to recent reports, the announcement is a striking inversion of how we’ve traditionally used software.
  • The rollout marks a major step toward the Copilot redesign the company first declared in September.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Opening the keynote at its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the manufacturer’s vision for its fresh “frontier ecosystem,” announcing Tuesday the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he described as “the new OS for work.”.

According to recent reports, the announcement is a striking inversion of how we’ve traditionally used software. Rather than an app like Word being the attraction and Clippy the assistant to help you use it, Microsoft envisions the new Copilot integrations will see agents driving things, with the software packages riding shotgun. Applications will become plugin components of the agent’s work, backed by an organizational knowledge layer that draws context from emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files. People will now be able to create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations directly in Copilot, with the resulting files remaining editable in their respective Office applications.

The rollout marks a major step toward the Copilot redesign the company first declared in September. Parts of that vision are now becoming “generally available,” as Nadella puts it, with autonomous agents and new governance tools arriving alongside them.

Copilot Autopilot (not to be confused with Windows Autopilot) is a “persistent, proactive agent for personal productivity” according to Microsoft. In a nutshell, Autopilot is a cloud-based autonomous AI agent that customers can delegate responsibilities to, not just single tasks. Autopilot can be authorized to work across services like email and calendars and complete tasks assigned to it as part of its role. Autopilot will use usage-based billing via Copilot Credits, but final pricing has not been unveiled ahead of general availability.

Also announced as generally available at the keynote speech was Microsoft IQ, an intelligence platform that houses Work IQ, a context layer that helps agents understand a firm’s communications, relationships, and ongoing work. Nadella described Work IQ as perhaps a company’s most valuable database: “It has a deep understanding of the people, their relationships to other people, your emails, your meetings, chats, projects that make up all the fabric of work.” Whether companies want autonomous agents to have access to internal documents and messaging data will have to be determined by their own internal IT review.

Copilot Workspaces is a collaborative environment currently available through Microsoft’s Frontier early-access program, but coming soon will be the ability to bring personal Autopilot agents into Workspaces. Early in the keynote address, Nadella remarked that “until now, AI interactions have mostly been single-player. Workspaces makes it a truly multiplayer experience, where people and agents drive towards a common goal, with shared context.”.

According to recent reports, trust, the third pillar of Microsoft’s new frontier ecosystem, was something that Nadella continued returning to during his presentation, and not in a way that some might expect. “We find ourselves in a place where alignment is elusive. Mechanistic understanding of these models is elusive. The question is: How can you even trust all this powerful technology? The reality is, by definition, you can’t,” he mentioned.

It has been revealed that in a departure from the norms of “AI is magic” corporate hype sentiment, Nadella conceded that the internal workings of AI thought processes remain difficult to understand, and models cannot be trusted to govern themselves, regardless of whether their answers are accurate. Nadella described the solution as “an architectural imperative to separate the supply of intelligence” from the authority granted to it. Microsoft says each Autopilot agent will have a unique ID, and administrators can restrict permissions or block it entirely. All agent activities are logged for human review, and Autopilot can ask for human approval before engaging in certain actions.

Industry observers note that the promised agent controls and admission that AI systems can’t always be trusted are meaningful, but Microsoft is asking businesses and people to place their trust in the company’s own safeguards instead, though the effectiveness of those safeguards against mistakes, rogue actions, or data exposure must still be demonstrated. In Microsoft’s view, the solution to untrustworthy intelligence is not to make AI agents trustworthy, but to control what they’re permitted to do. Businesses will need to decide how much autonomy they delegate to agents.

It has been revealed that along with the guardrails, Microsoft unveiled what it calls the “AI Transparency Initiative.” The effort has partnered with 40-plus major companies, including Adobe and MasterCard, to develop open, industry-wide standards for AI governance and security. Nadella described the initiative as a way for industry to “help establish an open standard that makes AI safer, more transparent, and more accessible.”.

According to recent reports, along with the other confirmed additions, Microsoft also announced expanding capabilities for Agent 365, its existing control plane for managing AI agents across enterprise environments. The newly introduced agent sheriff extends existing identity, security, and management systems to AI agents. Microsoft describes the objective as providing “observability at every layer of the stack.” Agent 365 offers governance controls over agent behavior in what Microsoft says is “autonomous in execution, but bounded and supervised.”.

Along with Agent 365 comes Agent 365 Business Analytics: “You can simply think of this as an ERP system of AI usage. You can see exactly what’s driving the spend and connect the spend to the outcomes that drive business value,” remarked Nadella. Customers will be able to see real-world costs associated with AI token-spend and compare those metrics to the value of work performed. Microsoft acknowledged that the estimations of assisted work hours are determined by a model, and not a direct measurement of time that may have been saved. This is a telling concession for Microsoft to make as businesses evaluate whether there will be an ROI on AI implementations, but according to Judson Althoff, CEO of Microsoft Commercial Business, “anything you can do with Claude or ChatGPT, you can do better with Copilot, for less.”.

Sources indicate that nadella offered only a brief acknowledgment of last week’s outage that disrupted access to services like Exchange Online and Teams for customers across the globe. “Last week was a reminder of how critical digital infrastructure is as the dial tone for the world,” he said. “We know the trust you place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously, and in that context I know we have work to do.”.

That statement was all the time the elephant in the room was given, but Microsoft did seem to acknowledge the public’s growing concern over data center projects by highlighting the previously discussed “community-first AI infrastructure plan.” Not a surprise in a presentation that asks organizations to extend more autonomy to software agents, at a time when Microsoft’s existing infrastructure is under increased scrutiny.

Industry News: I streamed GTA VI to my PC – it was awesome, even with lag

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You can stream GTA VI from your PS5 to a PC using PS Remote Play, then share your gameplay with friends through Discord’s screen-sharing feature.
  • Recent findings suggest that also: Can your PC run GTA VI?
  • I normally don’t preorder or buy games on Day One, but c’mon, it’s GTA VI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You can stream GTA VI from your PS5 to a PC using PS Remote Play, then share your gameplay with friends through Discord’s screen-sharing feature. I tested this setup on launch day and found that video quality remained consistent, although input lag made driving and shooting more difficult.

Recent findings suggest that also: Can your PC run GTA VI? The minimum requirements to expect.

I normally don’t preorder or buy games on Day One, but c’mon, it’s GTA VI. I was the first in my friend group to play on launch day; I was like a kid on Christmas morning. But I didn’t want to keep it all to myself, so I made plans to stream the game via Discord for a private watch party with my friends.

Using both the PS Remote Play app and Discord’s built-in screen sharing, I created an imperfect-but-workable solution — and got to have a bonkers good time with my friends despite GTA VI being a single-player experience.

In a recent development, the first few hours of GTA VI are absolutely Florida Man Simulator, and what better way to honor that than to find a jerry-rigged solution for sharing gameplay? The PS Remote Play app lets you stream gameplay to your smart TV or PC from your PS5 console, and then I simply used Discord’s screen-sharing feature to show the app to my friends.

I was most worried that both programs might compress the video feed into a pixelated, bitcrushed mess, but frequent check-ins from the peanut gallery assured me that everything was running smoothly and looking crisp.

Also: Need a GTA VI headset? Use headphones you own – with settings tweaks.

Using PS Remote Play did add a significant amount of input lag to my GTA VI gameplay, and while it’s easy enough to compensate for, it does make gunplay and driving slightly frustrating experiences.

As someone who is more used to real-world driving simulators like American Truck Simulator and Assetto Corsa Competizione, the driving already feels a touch too floaty and slippery, and the lag means you have to strategy every turn and stop well in advance to avoid sliding into the environment or slamming into the back of an NPC vehicle and getting the cops called on you. The gunplay lag is much easier to compensate for, especially if you keep your focus buffed and the meter filled to pull off trick shots and down multiple enemies without wasting ammo.

Streaming GTA VI to my friends also helped spark some interesting conversations about where we could see different influences from other Rockstar games, like the Heat system working very similarly to Red Dead Redemption 2’s Wanted mechanic: If you get caught committing a crime but manage to evade the police, that area of the map holds “heat,” so police and NPCs will be more vigilant and quicker to respond to reported crimes.

We also took plenty of time to just poke around Leonida and get a feel for the game world.

Also: Fake GTA 6 PC downloads are flooding the web.

It has been revealed that we went deep-sea fishing at night, searched underwater wrecks for treasures to sell, drove dirt bikes through the swamps, and watched several hours of in-game television (Right Wing on Weazel News is actually very good, and the Visit Leonida tourism ads are comedy gold). At some point, we fully abandoned the main storyline and even the side quests to go looking for Sasquatch and UFOs in the Grassrivers (the in-game equivalent of the Florida Everglades).

Sources indicate that as long as you have a decently fast internet connection, you’re likely to maintain consistent video quality while streaming GTA VI to friends on Discord or even to a live audience on YouTube or Twitch. Despite being captured by both PS Remote Play and Discord, the video feed wasn’t compressed much in my testing.

I don’t pay for Discord Nitro, so I streamed GTA VI in 720p — not the best video quality, but it’s good enough for a private watch party with my friends on our own server. If you do pay for Nitro, you’ll be able to stream in 1080p full HD to better show off GTA VI’s beautiful visuals (seriously, it is a breathtaking game, and I am very sad I can’t actually visit and dance with Rhonda & her pet iguana, Princess).

Also: Best early Black Friday gaming laptop deals.

Industry observers note that you could also use a program like OBS to capture gameplay footage from your PS5 without having to set up an expensive capture card, making it that much simpler to share GTA VI with a live audience on YouTube or Twitch. And even though there is a touch of noticeable lag when streaming via PS Remote Play, it’s not bad enough to detract from the fun, even after the Day 1 excitement faded.

CISA has added two new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation.

CVE-2026-134624 N-able Mail Assure (SpamExperts) Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) Vulnerability.

These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise.

Industry observers note that binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied.

While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities. CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria.

Aware of an exploited vulnerability not presently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form. Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.
